correctness.rationale: For every integer base b>=2 and odd n>=3, R_(n+2)=a+u and R_(n+6)=a+mu. Minimal coin number for coefficient t using denominations 1,m is c(t); u>m and the floor difference prove strict cost increase under t -> t+ha, yielding the complete Apéry set. Generator order identifies precisely a-1 and, for n>=5, km-1 as maximal Apéry indices; the n modulo 6 remainder comparison yields the Frobenius maximum; the Apéry sum produces the genus. Exactly one maximal Apéry element occurs at n=3, two thereafter. The attached checker independently recomputes all 18 example Apéry sets by residue-graph shortest paths and checks F, genus, pseudo-Frobenius sets, symmetry. These computations are auxiliary to the full proof; they do not substitute for infinite proof.
